title: Jennifer NDE 3044
content: It was about 10:30 Sunday night. I was in my backyard with my dog. It was his final potty break of the night. My husband was inside; he works nights and was supposed to be at work, but took this day off. After being outside for a few seconds, I heard some rustling in the live oak tree (it was over two hundred years old). I noticed my dog looking up in the tree and I also noticed some of the little branches moving around. It was dark outside and I got a panicked feeling. I opened the sliding glass door and yelled for my husband to get a flash light. A few second later, he came to the door and I repeated that something was in the tree and to get a light. I shut the door and looked at my dog (a dachshund). He looked back at me, and then I heard two popping noises. I realized at that point that the tree was going to fall. At that same point, my dog looked up at the tree and I yelled his name. I ran into the yard, scooped him up and starting running to get between the two houses. I didn't know which part of the tree was going to fall - I just knew it was going to happen. As I was running with my dog (granted at this point I only made it a few feet) I heard the terrible noise of the tree breaking. I repeated to myself with fear - I've got to get between the houses. At that point, - about six feet from my goal - it happened. A portion of the tree hit me. I felt several things at once. But the first thing I felt and saw when the tree hit my side was being in the middle of a bright light. It was around me and the edges were yellow and red. At that moment, I felt the presence of my granny and my grandpa and felt that they were there with me. I felt that they moved me to where I wouldn't be directly hit by the tree - like they saved me. I then thought, 'Wow, there really is a white light. This isn't how I'm supposed to die - I've got too many things to do.' It's as if time stood still because when I was back in my life, I saw the remaining part of the tree fall, hit the swing, and I watched it continue to fall on me. The actions were freeze framed, piece by piece - but my thoughts moved so fast. All the sounds and smells were frozen as each section moved. Once it all fell, all I heard was crickets and I remember looking at the sky, feeling panic and pain, wondering if I was dying and all the things I would leave. My husband came out and found me under the massive tree limb. I could hardly speak; I was getting cold and sweating. I whispered to him, after I asked him to call 911, 'Where is Lucky?' (My dog.) I thought he was crushed. My husband called for him and he emerged, unharmed, from the side of the house. I had further experiences in the ambulance and at the hospital. I can further explain. I will say that while at the hospital being wheeled into surgery I made an effort to look at myself in the mirrors that cornered the walls. It was as if I said goodbye and wanted to see if I looked how I knew I did. Dead.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Struck/pinned by a falling tree limb.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Time/scene described as freeze-framed while thoughts moved very fast; later said goodbye while being wheeled into surgery and looked at herself in mirrors, thinking she looked 'Dead.'
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Light and sensed deceased grandparents occurred at the moment of impact; no tunnel/OBE described; experience intertwined with slowed external events ('freeze framed').
stage_sequence.simultaneous_stage_detail: Perceived bright light and presence of grandparents while the tree impact and subsequent falling were experienced as freeze-framed externally.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Perception of the physical event as freeze-framed 'piece by piece' with frozen sounds/smells while thoughts moved very fast; later in hospital, while being wheeled into surgery, she looked at herself in mirrors as if saying goodbye and thought she looked 'Dead.'

It was around me and the edges were yellow and red.”; “It's as if time stood still...
